title: MLTD Assets Generated Manifest (content-addressed store)
description: Manifest of one asset_version inside generated/. The store keeps exactly one successful build per asset_version and references every payload by SHA-256 (content addressing). CLIENT AND ASSETS ARE INDEPENDENT VERSION AXES: 'asset_version' (assets axis) and 'source_client_version' (client axis, the client the official source bytes came from) are separate fields, and both are forbidden from containing '+' or '-assets-'. Combined identities such as '9.0.200+1077100' or 'client-9.0.200-assets-1077100' were retired by the owner (2026-09-27) and are rejected here so they cannot come back through a manifest.

asset_version.description: Assets axis only: the official asset cohort this release materialises (e.g. '1077100'). Combined identities are forbidden.

client_version.description: Always null on an assets-channel release. The APK built-in surface is delivered by the client repository; recording a client version here would re-couple the two axes.

source_client_version.description: Client axis only: the client version whose official asset bytes are the source of this release (e.g. '9.0.200'). It is context, not an identity: never concatenate it with asset_version.

source_commit.description: Commit of the official/pristine source snapshot used for this build.

translation_commit.description: Commit of the translation repository content that was applied.

generated_commit.description: Commit that already contained the generator inputs this build consumed. It is an ancestor of (or identical to) snapshot_commit by construction -- a later bot or documentation commit does not invalidate it.

ci_run_id.description: CI run identity that produced this release, either a run number or GitHub's <run_id>.<run_attempt>. Provenance only: null means the producer had no run context and never means 'unknown, guess one'. Never a version string, so a '+' or '-assets-' inside it is refused.

build_status.description: Only a successful build may write generated/. A 'failed' record documents the attempt without touching the store.

generated_at_utc.description: UTC timestamp of this build, informational only.

reuse_status_counts.description: Counts over the released entries only.

rejected_entries.description: Entries refused admission; they are reported with reasons and are NOT part of the release.

allOf.description: reuse_summary.entries must equal entry_count. Expressed as a shape check that JSON Schema can carry without arithmetic: both must equal len(entries). The tool enforces the equality in code; this clause pins the released-side invariant that suggested/blocked/untranslated/pending cannot be released.

not.description: A combined version anywhere in the identity fields is rejected. '+' and '-assets-' are the two markers the retired '9.0.200+1077100' / 'client-9.0.200-assets-1077100' identities used; the per-field patterns already forbid them, and this clause states the ban explicitly so it cannot be relaxed by accident.

entry.description: One generated artifact. It carries BOTH logical_path (the original game asset path the assets server keeps serving, e.g. 'event/001/title.unity3d') and object_path (where the bytes live in the content-addressed store).

channel.description: This store only publishes the assets-channel surface; APK built-in artifacts belong to the client repository.

asset_version.description: Must equal the manifest's asset_version; assets axis only.

client_version.description: Always null: separate axes, never a combined identity.

source_client_version.description: Client context that produced the official source bytes (e.g. '9.0.200').

ci_run_id.description: CI run identity that produced this release, either a run number or GitHub's <run_id>.<run_attempt>. Provenance only: null means the producer had no run context and never means 'unknown, guess one'. Never a version string, so a '+' or '-assets-' inside it is refused.

logical_key.description: Stable identity of the logical asset inside the translation repository.

logical_path.description: Original game asset path as the assets server serves it, e.g. 'event/001/title.unity3d'. Clean relative posix path: no leading slash, no backslash, no '..'.

resource_kind.description: What the payload is, because the logical path alone does not say. Every entry declares it and the producer refuses an entry without one: a surface that forgot to classify its output must fail the build, not be silently labelled 'other'.

source_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the OFFICIAL source asset. Equality of this value across versions is what makes reuse 'exact'.

translated_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the generated (localized) payload. Orthogonal to source_sha256: it can change while the source does not.

object_path.description: Store-relative content-addressed path, flat: objects/sha256/<full digest>. The optional <aa>/ segment is legacy compatibility: a manifest committed before the flat switch still resolves, and its shard is only pruned when no retained manifest names it.

artifact_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the stored bytes; must equal the digest embedded in object_path and the value listed in the release's checksums.txt.

reuse_status.description: Released manifests may only carry these two. 'exact' = source_sha256 unchanged (automatic reuse). 'verified-compatible' = source changed but a recorded verification authorises reuse. 'suggested' (path/name/text/visual similarity only) and 'blocked' (no evidence) are never released.

translation_status.description: Released manifests may only carry these three. 'accepted' = reviewed and approved; 'modified' = translated bytes differ from the previous release; 'reused' = identical translated bytes. 'untranslated' and 'pending' are never released. NOTE: a changed translation on an unchanged official source is reuse_status='exact' + translation_status='modified' -- it must NOT be relabelled 'verified-compatible'.

not.description: Combined client+assets identity is rejected in an entry too; the per-field patterns already forbid it and this clause states the ban explicitly.
